When questioned regarding his riding C L Chau stated that from a wide barrier he had been instructed to endeavour to obtain a midfield position with cover.  He said with the early stages of the event being run inside of standard time FORERUNNER settled towards the back of the field.  When questioned regarding his riding on the Home Turn and as to whether there was an opportunity to improve to the outside of CELESTIAL PATCH sooner than what he did C L Chau stated that the instructions issued by Trainer W K Mo preferred the horse securing an inside run due to the rail being in the "C+3” position.  He said with this in mind, when following CELESTIAL PATCH, he was of the opinion that from the 500 Metres that horse would shift out as it was under pressure and being ridden along.  He added that when CELESTIAL PATCH did not shift out and SIMPLE HEDGE then moved out from the rail he was unable to secure an inside run into the Home Straight.  He said after remaining behind CELESTIAL PATCH he then shifted FORERUNNER to the outside on entering the Home Straight where it finished the race off reasonably well.  Mr Mo confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with the manner in which Jockey Chau rode the horse.  After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Chau that, in their opinion, he should have shifted to the outside of CELESTIAL PATCH sooner than what he did, particularly having regard to the fact that his mount was positioned towards the rear of the field on the Home Turn.  He was further advised that in similar circumstances he should ride his mounts so as to leave no room for query.

After the event Y L Chung stated that with his mount stepping up in distance from the 1200 Metres to the 1650 Metres it raced keenly in the lead and refused to settle in the early stages.  He added that as a consequence VIGOR ELLEEGANT ran inside of standard time in the early stages despite his efforts to set a more sustainable pace.  He said having regard to the manner in which the horse raced in the early stages it weakened when placed under pressure in the Home Straight. Y L Chung was reprimanded in relation to using his whip in a manner where the hand holding the whip was above shoulder height on two occasions near the 150 Metres. The performance of VIGOR ELLEEGANT, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, VIGOR ELLEEGANT will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

K Teetan pleaded guilty to a charge under Rule 100(3(ii)(a) in that he used the whip in consecutive strides on at least 12 occasions prior to the 100 Metres.  After considering the relevant matters in respect of penalty which included the severity of the breach, a previous warning issued to Jockey Teetan regarding his whip hand being raised above shoulder height earlier during the meeting, the horse finishing in the first placing and also taking into consideration that the Rule was only introduced at the commencement of the season, he was issued with a two-meeting penalty.  As a consequence Jockey Teetan was suspended from riding in races for a period to commence on Thursday, 30 October 2025 and to expire on Monday, 3 November 2025 on which day he may resume race riding (2 Hong Kong racedays).  Sent for sampling post-race. <14/10/2025 Appeal – Jockey Karis Teetan> Jockey Karis Teetan has lodged a notice of appeal against the severity of the penalty imposed by the Racing Stewards at the Happy Valley race meeting held on 8 October 2025 for a breach of Rule 100(3)(ii)(a) when he rode KYRUS DRAGON in Race 9 that evening. Jockey Teetan pleaded guilty to the charge and was suspended from riding in races for two race meetings from 30 October 2025 to 2 November 2025 (both dates inclusive). The Stewards of the Jockey Club have granted a suspension of the penalty imposed on Jockey Teetan pending determination of his appeal. <6/11/2025 Result of Appeal Hearing - Jockey K Teetan>The Appeal lodged by Jockey Karis Teetan against the severity of the penalty imposed by the Racing Stewards at the Happy Valley race meeting held on 8 October 2025 for a breach of Rule 100(3)(ii)(a), namely a suspension from riding in races for two Hong Kong race days, was heard by the Appeal Panel at 3 p.m. today. After carefully considering all evidence presented during the appeal and submissions from both parties, the Appeal Panel allowed the appeal against the severity of the penalty.  The Panel ordered that the penalty be reduced to a suspension of riding in races for one Hong Kong race day on Wednesday 12 November 2025, together with a fine of HK$30,000. The Appeal Panel emphasised that this decision was made within the context of the current leniency period, which will cease to apply to race meetings from 12 November 2025, and should not be regarded as a precedent for future cases.

When questioned regarding his riding C L Chau stated that his instructions from a wide barrier were to settle the horse where comfortable.  He said in the early stages when caught wide and without cover he elected to restrain his mount in the Back Straight to ensure that he complied with his instructions to obtain cover.  He added that this resulted in SUPER JOY N FUN being settled towards the rear of the field.  When questioned regarding his riding making the Home Turn and in the early part of the Home Straight, particularly the vigour he used on SUPER JOY N FUN, C L Chau stated that after making the Home Turn he ensured his mount was balanced and encouraged SUPER JOY N FUN to change its lead leg.  He said when SUPER JOY N FUN did not change its lead leg in the early part of the Home Straight he continued to encourage the horse to improve but did not apply full vigour until near the 200 Metres after which SUPER JOY N FUN finished the race off reasonably well.  After considering the explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Chau that, in their opinion, he should have placed more pressure on his mount sooner than what he did to ensure that it obtained the best possible placing in the field.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
